title: Dead-letter queues
description: Learn about dead-letter queues for handling failed messages. Understand how to design robust error handling and recovery mechanisms.

data.text: Dead-letter queues (DLQs) hold messages that couldn't be processed successfully. They provide a safety net for failed messages, enabling monitoring, debugging, and recovery without blocking the main processing pipeline.
A DLQ is a secondary queue where messages are moved when they fail processing after a certain number of retries.

items: Messages that exceed max retry count go to DLQ
Prevents poison messages from blocking the queue
Enables separate monitoring and alerting
Allows manual inspection and reprocessing
Preserves message metadata for debugging

data.title: Why It Matters
data.text: Without DLQs, a single bad message can block your entire queue. DLQs isolate failures and keep your system running.
Messages are typically moved to the DLQ after exhausting retry policies.

items: Exceeded maximum retry count
Message validation failed (malformed data)
Consumer error during processing
Timeout processing the message
Routing failures (no matching consumer)
Always use DLQs in production systems
Include error context and stack traces
Set appropriate retry policies before DLQ
Monitor DLQ size and alert on spikes
Implement reprocessing mechanisms
TTL for DLQ messages to prevent unbounded growth

data.title: Don't Ignore
data.text: A growing DLQ indicates systemic problems. Set up monitoring and alerting to investigate when messages accumulate.
Have a strategy for dealing with messages that end up in the DLQ.

items.title: Investigate and Fix
items.description: Root cause analysis to prevent future failures. Fix bugs, update schemas, or adjust validation logic before reprocessing.

items.title: Reprocess After Fix
items.description: Once the issue is fixed, move messages back to the main queue for reprocessing. Ensure the fix addresses the root cause.

items.title: Manual Intervention
items.description: Some messages require manual review or data correction. Provide tools for operators to inspect and modify messages.

items.title: Discard After TTL
items.description: For non-critical messages, set a TTL and let them expire. Document why certain message types are safe to discard.

data.text: Configure retries appropriately to avoid premature DLQ placement.

items: Exponential backoff—gradually increase retry interval
Jitter—add randomness to avoid thundering herd
Max retry count—balance between persistence and giving up
Separate retry queues for different error types
Dead-letter only after sensible retry policy

data.text: Most messaging systems provide built-in DLQ support.

items: AWS SQS: Configure redrive policy for DLQ
RabbitMQ: Dead-letter exchange routing
Kafka: Separate topic for failed messages
Azure Service Bus: Dead-letter queue per queue/topic
Google Pub/Sub: Dead-letter topic configuration

data.title: Monitoring
data.text: Track DLQ metrics: message count, age, error types. Set up dashboards and alerts to respond quickly to problems.
